driver.text: Per WSJ, U.S. stocks jumped Monday even as Nvidia shares sank after its board launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, with the market rebounding from last week's rout (WSJ, 4:04 AM and 2:29 PM ET). Bloomberg reported a risk-on relief rally after President Trump said he is unlikely to launch broad attacks on Iran, with oil falling to its lowest since August (8:34 AM and 6:34 AM ET), and that most Treasuries fell as investors regained risk appetite (12:03 PM ET); WSJ reported U.S. and eurozone bond yields rose ahead of the inflation and rates outlook (2:33 PM ET). MarketWatch reported the rally is spreading beyond Big Tech, with Tuesday's CPI inflation report and a heavy slate of Federal Reserve speakers ahead (3:42 PM ET), and that AMD and Broadcom shares posted big gains Monday as Nvidia fell (1:33 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

cryptoDriver.text: The Block reported Bitcoin closed below its 50-week moving average as more than $1 billion in crypto long positions were liquidated over 24 hours (8:04 AM ET Nov 9); earlier it reported Bitcoin ETFs flipped negative for 2026 after a $1.28 billion outflow week, the worst since June (Nov 7). CoinDesk reported the Nvidia-led tech selloff weighed on crypto majors (6:42 AM ET).

items.headline: Nvidia board investigates reports CEO Jensen Huang was a spying target after affair
items.summary: Per WSJ, Nvidia's board is investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang was a spying target; Huang apologized for being unfaithful to his wife after an affair with an executive suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. WSJ also reported Nvidia shares fell close to 5% premarket (4:41 AM ET), and in its midday market coverage that U.S. stocks jumped even as Nvidia shares sank after the board launched the investigation. Nvidia closed down 4.27% on Nov 9. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.
